source.title: An Interpretability Illusion for Activation Patching of Arbitrary Subspaces

record.tranche_reason: The post reports IOI experiments showing that the effect of activation patching depends on whether a whole MLP layer or a learned subspace is patched, refining how subspace-level causal effects should be interpreted.
record.gate_note: The post describes and reports its own IOI patching experiments. Its account of the 26-head circuit and head roles is background from prior work, not a new test of those components. It does not knock out everything outside the circuit or test the seven head classes individually. Appendix results on recovering random directions and binary labels from MLP activations are not IOI-behaviour results.
record.test_reason: The post runs its own IOI patching experiments on GPT-2 small. It shows that DAS subspace patching can implicate MLP8, which lies outside the IOI circuit. It also shows that patching all of MLP8 does not hurt IOI, and that a residual-stream direction acts through the name-mover heads. This bears on whether other methods recover the same circuit (V4) and weakly on the circuit's composition (V1). It does not re-evaluate the circuit's faithfulness or completeness, so V5 is better treated as untested than as the record's main link.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors also state that they find the IOI paper's component-level analysis (MLP8 not in the circuit) convincing. They hold that activation patching remains useful at component level, but that subspace patching found by methods like DAS can fabricate effects and needs mechanistic validation.
record.recipe_differences: Uses DAS to learn arbitrary activation subspaces and then patches them, alongside whole-component and residual-stream patches; it does not reproduce the original 26-head circuit analysis. This is an Alignment Forum research post, not a replication.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported IOI effect changes with intervention scope (full MLP8 versus a learned direction), subspace composition (proj alone versus proj and null_proj together), and prompt positional information. The post does not report a broad sweep over evaluation metrics.

fits_no_version.finding: Linear probes on MLP activations recover random residual-stream directions (R^2 about 0.71) and binary features. DAS performance scales linearly with the number of MLP neurons it may use.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: MLP hidden layers linearly encode most residual-stream information, enabling spurious subspace-patching effects.

record.problems: The central IOI patch effects are mostly point estimates or qualitative comparisons without reported uncertainty. The post does not directly test the full circuit or the component-level claim that everything outside it can be removed without substantially changing IOI performance.
record.rows_left_out: No additional IOI-behaviour results omitted. The appendix's random-direction recovery and binary-classification results concern recoverability from MLP activations, not IOI behaviour; projection-distribution plots describe internal activations rather than the behaviour measured by the claim.

untested.parts: The full 26-head circuit, the seven classes individually, and faithfulness, completeness and minimality. Only MLP8's exclusion and the S-inhibition-to-name-mover signal are probed.
Not tested. Name movers are never ablated, though path patching mentions backup name-mover heads.
Circuit faithfulness and completeness under different ablations or metrics are not evaluated. The post only contrasts component-level and subspace-level patching of MLP8.
The DAS test set uses other templates and names, but the circuit is not tested across name orders, templates or prompts with more names.

missing.what: Path patching of the residual DAS direction: its effect runs through name-mover and backup name-mover heads, with attribution scores close to the unpatched run.
W_out times the MLP8 direction has cosine similarity 0.52 with the residual position direction (random baseline about 0.036).
missing.locator: Finding a position direction in MLP8; footnote 5

missing.what: Unpatched MLP8 output barely projects onto the position direction. Under opposite-position patches it writes a large value there, i.e. a dormant pathway is activated.
missing.locator: Patching along the subspace changes the output distribution of MLP8

record.verdict_notes: The record's V5-only linkage is replaced with V4 (and weak V1) links. The post's core result concerns method dependence of which components appear causal, not circuit faithfulness or completeness metrics. Results are point estimates without uncertainty. This is a non-peer-reviewed Alignment Forum post.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test the 26-head circuit, its seven classes and roles, or faithfulness, completeness and minimality; does not knock out everything outside the circuit.
Does not ablate the main name-mover heads to test whether backup heads take over.
Experiments are on GPT-2 small; does not test other models, sizes, checkpoints, or reuse of components on other tasks.
Does not compare circuit-finding methods, ablation types, or evaluation metrics as alternatives for recovering the circuit.

Tests sensitivity to patching a learned subspace versus a whole component and to subspace composition. Does not establish how much of ordinary IOI behaviour the 26-head circuit explains, or test a broad range of metrics or prompt distributions.

Tests candidate-direction patching on some IOI prompt patterns, templates and names, but does not test whether the claimed head circuit carries IOI across name orders, templates, or prompts with more names.

rows.subject: gpt2-small
rows.operation_detail: Patch a 1-dimensional residual-stream direction after layer 8 at the END token between prompts differing in repeated-name position.

conditions.value: residual stream after layer 8, END token
test set using other templates and names; ABB/BAB position patterns

rows.note: The authors use this as a within-circuit candidate direction and comparator for the MLP8 result.
rows.check: Relinked from V5. The DAS direction after layer 8, between the S-inhibition and name-mover heads, flips predictions about 80% of the time. Path patching (not recorded as a row) shows it acts via the name-mover and backup name-mover heads, as the circuit's roles predict.

source_check.locator_found: Distributed alignment search, paragraphs describing optimization and held-out prediction flips.

rows.subject: gpt2-small
rows.operation_detail: Patch full MLP8 activations between prompts with opposite position information.
rows.measure: Change in logit difference between the correct and incorrect name
rows.locator: Finding a position direction in MLP8
rows.note: The authors describe the full-layer patch as helpful for the task, in contrast to the learned direction patch.
rows.check: Relinked from V5. Patching all of MLP8 raises logit difference by about 0.4, i.e. it does not hurt the task. This matches MLP8 not being in the circuit. No baseline is needed beyond the unpatched run.

source_check.locator_found: Finding a position direction in MLP8, paragraph comparing full-activation and direction patches.

rows.subject: gpt2-small
rows.operation_detail: Patch the 1-dimensional DAS direction in MLP8 between prompts with opposite position information.
rows.measure: Change in logit difference between the correct and incorrect name
rows.baseline: Full MLP8 patch increases logit difference by ~0.4
rows.value: decreases by ~1.3; described as a ~3x stronger effect in the opposite direction
rows.locator: Finding a position direction in MLP8
rows.note: The result is the post's central example of a subspace patch having a different effect from patching its whole component.
rows.check: Relinked from V5. A DAS subspace patch in MLP8, a component outside the circuit, cuts logit difference by about 1.3. The authors say MLP8 would thus 'appear as a significant circuit component', so the method implicates a non-circuit component. The baseline is the full MLP8 patch (+0.4).

source_check.correct: State for V4: absent. Full MLP8 patching increases logit difference by approximately 0.4; DAS-direction patching decreases it by approximately 1.3 and falsely implicates a component outside the circuit.
source_check.locator_found: Finding a position direction in MLP8; Patching along the subspace changes the output distribution of MLP8.
source_check.problem: The logit-change sign reverses relative to full-component patching, but V4 concerns agreement in circuit recovery; that agreement is absent rather than reversed.

rows.subject: gpt2-small
rows.operation_detail: Patch the entire residual stream after layer 8 at the END token.

conditions.value: residual stream after layer 8, END token

rows.locator: Finding a position direction in MLP8
rows.note: The authors also say the MLP8 direction's logit-difference effect is about 30–40% of the logit difference lost under this residual-stream patch.
rows.check: This is a reference point used to scale the MLP8 effect: patching the whole residual stream drops performance from about 99% to about 30%. It is not a test of any version. Its 'partial' state is meaningless.

rows.subject: gpt2-small
rows.operation_detail: Patch only the component of the MLP8 DAS direction orthogonal to the nullspace of Wout (proj).
rows.baseline: Patching the full MLP8 DAS direction
rows.value: effect decreases by a factor of ~3.3x
rows.note: The post reports a weaker effect for this restricted patch, not a separate absolute logit-difference value.
rows.check: A mechanistic decomposition of the MLP8 artefact (proj component alone gives an effect about 3.3x weaker). It explains the illusion rather than measuring the circuit or the method's agreement with it.

rows.subject: gpt2-small
rows.operation_detail: Patch the 2-dimensional subspace spanned by proj and null_proj.

conditions.value: subspace spanned by proj and null_proj

rows.value: loses the effect of the MLP8 direction patch
rows.note: The authors explicitly say this larger subspace patch loses the direction patch's effect.
rows.check: Part of the same decomposition analysis: patching the 2-D span of proj and null_proj loses the effect. The 'absent' state does not refer to any version's effect.

rows.subject: gpt2-small
rows.operation_detail: Train a DAS subspace on randomly sampled MLP weights and biases, then add the patched-versus-unpatched random-MLP output difference to the real MLP8 output.

conditions.value: norm of output activations matched to MLP8
random MLP is not substituted for MLP8

rows.value: reduces logit difference even more than the MLP8 direction
rows.locator: DAS subspaces exist in MLPs with random weights
rows.note: No numerical effect size is stated.
rows.check: Relinked from V5. DAS finds an effective subspace even in an MLP with random weights placed at MLP8. So subspace patching can implicate a position in the network regardless of what it computes. No numeric effect size is given.

source_check.correct: State for V4: absent. A DAS subspace in a norm-matched random MLP reduces logit difference more than the MLP8 direction; no numerical effect size is stated.
source_check.locator_found: DAS subspaces exist in MLPs with random weights, experimental setup and result paragraph.
source_check.problem: The random-MLP and MLP8 directions change logits in the same direction; the result shows failure of faithful circuit recovery, not a reversed circuit effect.

rows.subject: gpt2-small
rows.operation_detail: Patch a direction formed from the difference between mean prompts with the repeated name first versus second.

conditions.value: residual stream after layer 8, END token

rows.measure: Causal effect of patching on model predictions
rows.value: smaller causal effect; the two directions have ~0.85 cosine similarity
rows.note: The cosine similarity is a separate reported comparison; the post gives no numeric causal-effect size for this direction.
rows.check: Compares two ways of constructing the residual direction (mean difference vs DAS; cosine similarity about 0.85). This is a method-internal comparison with no numeric causal effect, not a test of a version.

relationships.condition: GPT-2 small, ABB/BAB position-patched IOI prompts
relationships.reason: Whole-MLP8 patching does not hurt IOI (R2), consistent with MLP8 being outside the circuit. The position direction between the S-inhibition and name-mover heads flips predictions about 80% of the time (R1) and, per the text, acts via the name movers. Narrow support only.
relationships.display_finding: Patching the position direction between S-inhibition and name-mover heads flipped predictions about 80% of the time through name movers, while patching the whole MLP8 did not impair IOI.

source_check.label: supports
source_check.condition: GPT-2 small, ABB/BAB position-patched IOI prompts
source_check.reason: R1 and path patching support the position-information channel through name movers; R2 is consistent with MLP8 being outside the circuit. Support is limited to these tested components.

relationships.condition: DAS run on the residual stream after layer 8
relationships.reason: The learned direction flips about 80% of predictions and acts through name-mover and backup name-mover heads, consistent with the circuit (R1; path-patching detail is from the text).
relationships.display_finding: The learned direction flipped about 80% of predictions and acted through name-mover and backup name-mover heads.

source_check.condition: DAS run on the residual stream after layer 8
source_check.reason: R1 identifies a position direction whose effect is validated as acting largely through the original circuit's name-mover and backup name-mover heads.

relationships.condition: DAS subspace patching on MLP components (MLP8, or a random MLP at that position)
relationships.reason: Subspace patching implicates MLP8 (logit difference about -1.3), a non-circuit component that whole-component patching clears (+0.4). A random MLP at that position does likewise. The authors call this an illusion that needs extra validation (R2, R3, R7).
relationships.display_finding: Subspace patching implicated MLP8 with logit difference about −1.3, whereas whole-component patching gave +0.4; a random MLP at the same position produced a similar illusion.

source_check.condition: DAS subspace patching on MLP components (MLP8, or a random MLP at that position)
source_check.reason: R2, R3 and R7 demonstrate disagreement where V4 predicts essentially the same circuit: subspace patching implicates excluded MLP8 and even a random MLP through a normally dormant pathway.

relation.reason: The post reports its own IOI interventions and mechanistic validation bearing on V1 and V4.

tranche.reason: Its experiments show that subspace patching can implicate non-circuit components, directly qualifying method-independent circuit identification.

source_check.notes: The post supports a circuit submechanism without retesting all 26 heads or the full faithfulness, completeness and minimality criteria. Numerical results attributed to other studies in the combined statements were outside this check.

statements.correction: V4 label for MLP-component DAS: challenges. MLP8 direction: approximately −1.3 logit-difference change. Full MLP8 patch: approximately +0.4. Random-MLP direction: greater logit-difference reduction than the MLP8 direction.
statements.problem: The facts attributed to this post are correct, but the MLP condition directly contradicts V4's method-independent recovery claim and warrants challenges.

statements.correction: Residual-stream direction: approximately 80% prediction flips, acting largely through name-mover and backup name-mover heads. Removing the MLP8 direction's nullspace component reduces its logit-difference effect by approximately 3.3-fold. Interchange-accuracy comparison: not reported.
statements.problem: The location, scope and decomposition findings are supported. This post does not report interchange accuracy or establish its divergence from fractional logit-difference decrease.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: GPT-2 small, tested opposite-position IOI prompts and MLP8/residual-stream patch settings
reader_labels.reason: The reported effects differ across patch scope and subspace choice: whole-MLP8 patching is helpful, the learned MLP8 direction patch decreases logit difference, and restricting or enlarging the patched subspace changes or removes that effect (R2–R6).
